# relay_valkey_cluster (Resource)

A managed Valkey cluster. Creating, updating and destroying wait for the cluster to settle. Changing `name`, `workspace_id` or `mode` replaces the cluster and its data; use `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "relay_valkey_cluster" "sessions" {
  workspace_id = relay_workspace.prod.id
  name         = "sessions"
  version      = "9.1"

  storage = {
    size = "8Gi"
  }

  nodes = {
    cache = {
      count     = 2
      cloud     = "aws"
      region    = "us-east-1"
      tier      = "RC20"
      resources = {}
      autoscaling = {
        enabled  = true
        min_tier = "RC10"
        max_tier = "RC40"
      }
    }
  }

  parameters = {
    "maxmemory-policy" = "allkeys-lru"
  }
}

resource "relay_valkey_cluster" "leaderboard" {
  workspace_id        = relay_workspace.prod.id
  name                = "leaderboard"
  mode                = "cluster"
  shards              = 3
  replicas_per_shard  = 1
  deletion_protection = true

  storage = {
    size = "28Gi"
    autoscale = {
      enabled     = true
      max_storage = "100Gi"
    }
  }

  nodes = {
    shards = {
      count     = 6
      cloud     = "aws"
      region    = "us-east-1"
      tier      = "RC40"
      resources = {}
    }
  }

  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Cluster name, unique in the workspace.
- `nodes` (Attributes Map) The cluster's single node group, keyed by a label you choose. Renaming it replaces the cluster. In `cluster` mode `count` must equal `shards * (1 + replicas_per_shard)`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--nodes))
- `workspace_id` (String) Workspace the cluster belongs to.

### Optional

- `default_connections` (Attributes) Relay-managed users the platform creates once the cluster is running, each with a Relay connection that uses it: one read-only, one read-write and one admin. Omitted on create, all three are created, as the Relay console does; omitted afterwards, the current value is kept. Changing a role on an existing cluster creates it, or deletes its connection and then its user, without replacing the cluster; a user whose roles were changed outside Relay is kept. The platform applies a change after the apply returns. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--default_connections))
- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) While `true`, the platform refuses to delete the cluster, and `terraform destroy` or a replacement fails before deleting it. Turning it on needs deletion protection enabled for the organization. Turning it off needs the `org.deletion_protection.disable` permission, which the owner and admin roles hold.
- `keep_backups_on_destroy` (Boolean) Keep the cluster's backups when it is destroyed.
- `mode` (String) `replication` runs one primary and its replicas. `cluster` shards the keyspace across `shards` primaries, each with `replicas_per_shard` replicas. Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `parameters` (Map of String) Valkey settings, for example `maxmemory-policy`. An empty map resets them to defaults; omitting the attribute leaves them unmanaged. Settings the platform manages, such as `maxmemory` or `port`, are rejected. The platform stores canonical names (lower case, aliases resolved); the spelling you configure is kept in state when it maps to the stored name.
- `replicas_per_shard` (Number) Replicas behind each shard's primary, 0-4. Only in `cluster` mode; omitted means 0.
- `restore` (Attributes) Creates the cluster from another cluster's backups instead of empty. The platform picks the backup and starts the cluster with the source's settings; the provider then applies the configured nodes and settings. `mode`, `version` when set, and the node group label must match the source's. Only read on create: changing it replaces the cluster, while adding it to or removing it from an existing cluster changes nothing. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--restore))
- `shards` (Number) Primaries the keyspace is split across, 3-100. Required in `cluster` mode and not allowed in `replication` mode. Changing it reshards in place, together with the node group's `count`.
- `storage` (Attributes) Volume size and autoscaling for the whole cluster: every node holds the same data, so every node's volume has this size. Omit the block and the platform picks the size, which the next read reports; once it is set, removing the whole block keeps the current size and autoscaling, so remove `autoscale` alone to turn it off. Disk type, IOPS and throughput stay per node group. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--storage))
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `version` (String) Valkey version, for example `9.1`. Omit it and the platform picks one, which the next read reports. It cannot change here: upgrades go through Relay's upgrade flow, and a plan that changes it fails.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation time, RFC 3339.
- `endpoint_host` (String) Public read-write endpoint host. Empty until the platform publishes it.
- `endpoint_port` (Number) Public read-write endpoint port.
- `id` (String) Cluster ID.
- `phase` (String) Lifecycle phase after the last apply.
- `phase_message` (String) Detail for the phase.
- `private_endpoints` (Attributes List) Private endpoints by role, when private access is enabled. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--private_endpoints))
- `public_endpoints` (Attributes List) Public endpoints by role. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--public_endpoints))
- `ready_nodes` (Number) Nodes ready.
- `storage_status` (Attributes) Volume size the platform has grown to via `storage.autoscale`, when above `storage.size`. Null until it grows. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--storage_status))
- `total_nodes` (Number) Nodes expected.
- `updated_at` (String) Last change time, RFC 3339.

<a id="nestedatt--nodes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `nodes`

Required:

- `cloud` (String) Cloud the group runs in: `aws`, `gcp` or `azure`.
- `region` (String) Region the group runs in, for example `us-east-1`.
- `resources` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--nodes--resources))
- `tier` (String) Relay Cache machine catalog name, for example `RC10`. CPU and memory are derived from it; an unknown name is rejected. With `autoscaling` enabled the platform moves the group away from it without changing this value, reported in `current_tier`.

Optional:

- `autoscaling` (Attributes) Moves the group one tier at a time between `min_tier` and `max_tier`; the node count never changes. `tier` keeps the configured value, so a move never shows as drift; the tier the group runs at is `current_tier`. Omitting this block, or removing it from a config that had it, turns autoscaling off. Needs the `compute_autoscale` feature, and the Free plan cannot enable it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--nodes--autoscaling))
- `count` (Number) Nodes in the group. In `replication` mode, one primary and `count - 1` replicas.

Read-Only:

- `current_tier` (String) Tier the group runs at after autoscaling moved it. Null while `autoscaling` is off or before the platform first reports it.

<a id="nestedatt--nodes--resources"></a>
### Nested Schema for `nodes.resources`

Read-Only:

- `cpu` (String) CPU request derived from `tier`.
- `memory` (String) Memory request derived from `tier`.


<a id="nestedatt--nodes--autoscaling"></a>
### Nested Schema for `nodes.autoscaling`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Turn compute autoscaling on for the group.

Optional:

- `max_tier` (String) Highest tier the group may move up to. Required when `enabled` is true.
- `min_tier` (String) Lowest tier the group may move down to. Required when `enabled` is true, and `tier` must lie between `min_tier` and `max_tier`.
- `respect_maintenance_window` (Boolean) Hold moves up until the cluster's maintenance window too. Moves down always wait for it.
- `rules` (Attributes List) Metrics that move the group, at most 8, each metric once. Omit it for the Relay default policy: `cpu` and the engine's memory metric, up above 75 and down below 40. The group moves up when any rule stays above `scale_up_above` for `scale_up_window`, and down when every rule stays below `scale_down_below` for `scale_down_window`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--nodes--autoscaling--rules))
- `scale_down_window` (String) How long every rule must stay below its threshold before the group moves down, a duration such as `6h`. Omitted, the platform waits 24 hours.
- `scale_up_window` (String) How long a rule must stay above its threshold before the group moves up, a duration such as `5m`. Omitted, the platform waits 10 minutes.

<a id="nestedatt--nodes--autoscaling--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `nodes.autoscaling.rules`

Required:

- `metric` (String) Metric from the engine's autoscaling catalog: `cpu`, `memory`, `valkey.memory`, `valkey.ops` and `valkey.clients`. The platform rejects any other.
- `scale_down_below` (Number) Value below which the group moves one tier down. Must be lower than `scale_up_above`.
- `scale_up_above` (Number) Value above which the group moves one tier up, in the metric's unit. A percentage is at most 100.




<a id="nestedatt--default_connections"></a>
### Nested Schema for `default_connections`

Optional:

- `admin` (Boolean) The admin user and its connection. Omitted, it is `true` on create and keeps its current value afterwards.
- `readonly` (Boolean) The read-only user and its connection. Omitted, it is `true` on create and keeps its current value afterwards.
- `readwrite` (Boolean) The read-write user and its connection. Omitted, it is `true` on create and keeps its current value afterwards.


<a id="nestedatt--restore"></a>
### Nested Schema for `restore`

Required:

- `source_database_id` (String) ID of the cluster to restore from, in the same workspace and with backups. For a destroyed cluster whose backups were kept, the ID it had.

Optional:

- `target_time` (String) Recover up to this instant, RFC 3339, for example `2026-10-31T12:00:00Z`. It replays the source's AOF archive, so it needs `mode = "replication"`, a source that still exists with `pitr_window_days` on its backup schedule, and an instant inside that window. Omit it to restore the latest backup.


<a id="nestedatt--storage"></a>
### Nested Schema for `storage`

Optional:

- `autoscale` (Attributes) Grows the cluster's volumes past `size`, up to `max_storage`, when disk usage crosses `threshold_percent`. Omitting this block, or removing it from a config that had it, disables autoscaling. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--storage--autoscale))
- `size` (String) Minimum volume size for persistence, Kubernetes quantity. Omit it to use the tier's storage. The platform raises the volume to at least 1.5 times the node's memory and never lowers it, so after a refresh this holds the size it is at; a configured value at or below that plans no change, and a larger one grows the volume. With `autoscale` enabled the platform may grow the volume past it, reported in `storage_status`.

<a id="nestedatt--storage--autoscale"></a>
### Nested Schema for `storage.autoscale`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Turn storage autoscaling on for the cluster.

Optional:

- `increase_percent` (Number) Percent to grow the volume by on each trigger. `0` or omitted uses the platform default of 20; otherwise 10-100.
- `max_storage` (String) Ceiling the platform will not grow past, Kubernetes quantity. Required when `enabled` is true, and must be at least `size`.
- `threshold_percent` (Number) Disk-usage percent that triggers a grow. `0` or omitted uses the platform default of 80; otherwise 50-95.



<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import relay_valkey_cluster.sessions <workspace_id>/<cluster_id>
```
